text:
maya: Quick design check — compact streaming layout prototype attached. Main question: move Stop/Regenerate into the message action rail vs inline next to the stream? Also token counter: pill collapsed by default or always visible? aria-live behavior for streaming partials? joel: I lean inline stop. closer to the content and easier for keyboard reach. rail feels too far in compact view. :thinking: elaine: a11y: important to set aria-live="polite" on the live region and then announce a single "Generation complete" when finished. avoid announcing every chunk. keyboard focus should move to the generated message when done. sam: infra note: inline stop will affect event layering — we need to ensure the stop click cancels the backend stream cleanly. CSS stacking might be fiddly (z-index). kai: token counter idea: condensed pill showing current/limit (eg 120/2048) and show full breakdown on hover or via a tooltip. saves horizontal space. maya: copy tweak: prefer explicit copy — change "Stop" to "Stop generation" and "Regenerate" to "Regenerate response". longer but clearer for non-technical users, esp mobile. joel: agree on copy. Implementation question: should Stop be aria-pressed? feels like a single action, not a toggle. elaine: do not use aria-pressed for this. aria-pressed implies a toggle. Use role="button" (native button if possible) with an aria-label that includes context e.g. "Stop generation for this message". designbot: quick perf check — adding inline stop increases median render time by ~8ms in the compact layout, end-to-end still within budget. maya: token meter visual: use color-blind friendly palette (avoid red/green pairs). always include a text fallback such as "120/2048 tokens" for assistive tech. sam: prompt library quick-insert: options — drag-to-draft vs inline insert. dragging adds complexity on mobile. propose inline insert + long-press preview on mobile. kai: accessibility code snippet suggestion: ```html
…partial tokens…
``` joel: also: debounce aria announcements for streaming chunks to avoid screen reader spam. batch updates every ~300ms and only announce final completion message. maya: proposed decision list: 1) Inline Stop/Regenerate next to stream, 2) Token counter = collapsed pill + hover/tooltip details, 3) aria-live batching at 300ms + single "Generation complete" announcement, 4) prompt library = inline insert with long-press preview on mobile. Any objections? elaine: +1 :+1: one nit — don't announce token count automatically; surface it on request (keyboard shortcut or tooltip activation) to reduce noise. sam: I'll open a ticket for the z-index/CSS clipping and add an integration test for cancellation behavior. joel: I'll take the aria debounce work and add unit tests for the announce cadence. kai: I'll own the token tooltip + accessible text fallback. maya: I'll update the Figma mock and post the new frames here when ready. thanks all :rocket: maya: follow-up: pinging for final sign-off tomorrow after PRs land.
